rejected_rule.statement: The mere fact that one co-owner was in occupation of the entirety of a house which was owned in common and purported to execute deeds in respect of the entirety for a period of over ten years does not lead to the presumption of an ouster in the absence of evidence to show that the other co-owners had knowledge of the transactions.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: The same principle is affirmed in Sideris v. Simon [(1945) 46 N. L. R. 273.] and Ummu Ham v. Koch [(1946) 47 N. L. R. 107.]
